cards.explanation: The answer is the Son of David. Jesus opens with, “How can the scribes say that the Christ is the Son of David?” (Mark 12:35). David was Israel's king (2 Samuel 5:3), and the scribes tie the Christ to his family. Hold on to that, friends, because Jesus is about to do something with it.

The answer is to sit at His right hand. David, Israel's king (2 Samuel 5:3), is speaking by the Holy Spirit, and the words are “Sit at My right hand until I put Your enemies under Your feet.” (Mark 12:36). A seat at the right hand, friends.

The answer is False. Mark 12:37 says “…the large crowd listened to Him with delight.” That's a big crowd, and they're happy to be there. If I had a crowd listening to me with delight, I'd probably need a lie down on my gold base.

The word is honor. The scribes want the chief seats in the synagogues and “…the places of honor at banquets.” (Mark 12:39). They want the best spot in the room. I spent years in a junk drawer, so I'd settle for any spot that isn't under a takeout menu.

The word is show. Jesus says they “…for a show make lengthy prayers.” (Mark 12:40). Right before that, He says they defraud widows of their houses. Those words are heavy, friends, and Jesus doesn't soften them.

The answer is greater condemnation. Jesus says, “These men will receive greater condemnation.” (Mark 12:40). It comes right after He names what the scribes do. It's a serious line, so I'll leave it right there.

The answer is two small copper coins. The text says one poor widow “…put in two small copper coins…” (Mark 12:42). That's all there is: two little coins. Keep your eye on them, friends, because Jesus is about to say something big about them.

The answer is True. Jesus says it plainly: “Truly I tell you, this poor widow has put more than all the others into the treasury.” That includes the many rich people who put in large amounts (Mark 12:41). He calls His disciples to Him to say it.

The answer is that she gave all she had to live on. That's the reason Jesus gives. He says, “For they all contributed out of their surplus, but she out of her poverty has put in all she had to live on.” (Mark 12:44). The others gave from what was left over, and she gave everything she had to live on. Two coins, friends, and Jesus says it's more than all of them.
